Tesla hasn't released any actual data sheets for their motors; So, take everything I say with a grain of salt. In my experience 3 phase motors tend to be most efficient around 4000 rpm. We use gearing to put that range where most people do their driving which is around 60 mph or 100 kph. So, theoretically the motor would be running most efficiently at 60 mph. However, wind resistance roughly squares with speed. Meaning that if you're going 10 mph and have 10 newtons of wind resistance than going 20 mph means you now have 100 newtons of wind resistance. So, to answer your question the motor is not operating at peak efficiency, but because of the reduced drag less power is required to go the same distance even factoring in the motor efficiency loss.

Devaluation can be a short-term band-aid for economies that when at least parts of the underlying structure are fundamentally solid.

Greece's problems have growing slowly for around 100 years now. It's fundamentals have become centralization, patronage, and protectionism. Moving to the drachma might help for a few years but unless they reform their overall economic approach, they'll just bleed worse when you rip off the band-aid.

Look, I'm not saying Greece is the great, evil, socialist empire. Good people can make what look like reasonable decisions at the time, and only later see they're at the bottom of a hole with nothing but a shovel.

I'm also not saying they didn't get seriously screwed by some of the initial conditions of the bailout. A tough stance needed to be taken, but there were plenty of private lenders pouring money into Greece even though there were already red flags all over the place. They were looking for some big rewards and ended up getting protected from a large part of the risk.

Regardless, there is a long road ahead. An economic system that has been developing for close to a century can't be undone overnight.
